lede: Martinsville starts Christmas with a light parade that ends at Jimmy Nash City Park, where the Festival of Lights keeps glowing until New Year's Day.
celebrates: The City of Martinsville opens the season with the Home for the Holidays Christmas Light Parade, an evening of lights, floats, Christmas music and a visit from Santa. The parade travels East Washington Street, turns onto Home Avenue and ends at Jimmy Nash City Park, just as the Festival of Lights kicks off and lights up the park. That lower park display stays up until New Year's Day. Old Town Park at Waverly hosts Santa in the Park, and neighboring Mooresville adds a downtown tree lighting at Bicentennial Park and a Victorian Christmas Festival with trolley stops.
lastyear: On Saturday, November 29, 2025, Jimmy Nash City Park held the Winter Wonderland Festival of Lights Park Lighting Ceremony from 6:30 to 8:30 pm, free to the public. The city's calendar listed a visit with Santa Claus, crafts and games, a Christmas song sing-along, and holiday treats from food trucks and select vendors. The 2026 version moves to Saturday, November 28, and follows the Home for the Holidays parade, so families can watch the floats and then walk straight into the park.
facts: Festival of Lights takes place each year at Jimmy Nash City Park, at 360 N. Home Avenue, on the Saturday after Thanksgiving. Morgan County's visitor bureau says the event includes a visit with Santa and live music from the Martinsville Community Band. It kicks off a weeks-long holiday lights display in the lower part of the park that stays up until New Year's Day. The park closes at 9 pm, and a sensor opens the gate for anyone still inside at closing time.
trains: Martinsville has no Christmas train of its own, and our guide has no train ride in Morgan County. The closest listing is Nickel Plate Express in Forest Park in Noblesville, on the north side of the Indianapolis area, which runs trains in the Christmas season including the Reindeer Express. It is a longer drive than most Martinsville events, so check that page for dates and ticket details, and book early because train seats sell out.

faq: When is the Martinsville Christmas parade in 2026?

The Home for the Holidays Christmas Light Parade is Saturday, November 28, 2026, at 6 pm on Washington Street in Martinsville. It is free to watch. The route turns onto Home Avenue and ends at Jimmy Nash City Park, where the Festival of Lights opens with Santa, so most families stay for the park afterward.
What is the Festival of Lights at Jimmy Nash City Park?

The Winter Wonderland Festival of Lights is the park's lighting ceremony on the Saturday after Thanksgiving, with Santa, crafts, games and live music. It starts a holiday light display in the lower park that stays up until New Year's Day. The park is at 360 N. Home Avenue and closes at 9 pm.
Where can kids meet Santa in Martinsville?

Santa makes a special visit at the Home for the Holidays parade and the Festival of Lights at Jimmy Nash City Park on November 28. He also visits Old Town Park at Waverly for Santa in the Park on December 12, and the Mooresville Victorian Christmas Festival on December 5. Each card lists its own time and link.

All five events on this page are free. The parade, the Festival of Lights ceremony, Santa in the Park and both Mooresville events do not charge admission, though the Festival of Lights asks for donations and food truck treats cost extra. Check each card for the host's own notes before you go.
Is there a Christmas train near Martinsville?

Martinsville has no Christmas train ride. The closest in our guide is Nickel Plate Express in Noblesville, which runs the Reindeer Express in the Christmas season and sells tickets ahead of time. For lights and Santa closer to home, Jimmy Nash City Park is the easiest choice and costs nothing.
